parameters: \n<Priest>This morning, at seven o' clock. At Bagumbayan.
Jose Rizal.
The crowd does not react at first. The words do not
make sense. Then a woman begins to cry — not loudly,
but with the particular sound of someone who is crying
for more than one thing.
The priest reads the telegram. Rizal was executed at
7:03 AM by firing squad. His body was claimed by the
friars. There will be no public burial. His family has
been denied permission to hold a wake.
The church bell begins to toll. Slow. Someone inside
has started it. The priest turns and goes inside.
\n<Florante>He did not join us, you know that? He did not sign.
He said the people were not ready.
\n<Florante>But they killed him anyway.
\n<Mariano Trias>They were more afraid of him than of a thousand of us.
\n<Mariano Trias>He did not fight. He did not hold a gun. But there is
no going back now.
\n<Mariano Trias>All discussion is over. All compromise is over.
Jose Rizal was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan
(now Luneta) on the morning of 30 December 1896. He had
refused the Katipunan's offer to rescue him from prison.
Though he never joined the revolution, his novels —
Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo — and his
execution made him the most powerful symbol of the
cause. His martyrdom ended any possibility of
compromise between the revolution and Spain.
